page: Amazon Web Services t4g.small is a burstable virtual machine configured on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an arm64 AWS Graviton processor built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. The allocation provides 2 physical cores mapped to 2 vCPUs without multithreading, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 2.0 GB, establishing a 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware profile includes AES cryptographic acceleration but offers no onboard GPU accelerators or bundled local storage.

Benchmark evaluations highlight performance characteristics tailored to transient and low-intensity tasks. In stress-ng execution, the single-core CPU throughput reached 1519.08, which aligns with mid-range baselines, while multi-core performance registered at 3011.46. Memory subsystems delivered uncached read bandwidth of 34.1 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 15.29 GB/sec. Across operational workloads, the instance achieved 2.14 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 2.1 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-threaded gzip compression measured 20.34 GB/sec, alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 12.23 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on cost-efficient capacity for workloads with variable utilization profiles. Operating under a CPU credit model with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, sustained compute bursts rely on accumulated credits. Persistent storage requires network-attached volumes, as no local NVMe is present. The instance is suited for development sandboxes, staging environments, build workers, low-traffic web endpoints, and lightweight background microservices.
